summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with sepsis likely originating from a urinary source, given his history of nephrolithiasis and presenting symptoms of fever, flank pain, and urinary symptoms. He was tachycardic and febrile on arrival, with leukocytosis and elevated lactate, consistent with severe sepsis. Imaging showed a nonobstructing left staghorn calculus and mild perinephric fat stranding, suggesting pyelonephritis. He received IV vancomycin and cefepime initially, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin after Klebsiella pneumoniae was identified. His course was complicated by an elevated INR of 4.0 on admission, which was managed by holding warfarin temporarily and later reducing the dose to 4 mg daily. He developed transient acute kidney injury after restarting torsemide 50 mg daily, leading to volume depletion; this was corrected by switching to PRN low-dose torsemide based on weight changes. He improved clinically, became afebrile, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics and adjusted anticoagulation with follow-up planned for urology and INR monitoring.
